bon.name: Bön
bon.desc: Emerging from the religious traditions of $tibet_region$ before the arrival of $buddhist$, it became very influenced by $tibetan_buddhism$. It is especially close to the $SECT_NYIGMA_NAME$, but still preserves many pre-$buddhist$ elements. Its teachings focus on Karma and rebirth, and the ways of achieving enlightenment.

mahayana.name: Eastern Buddhism
mahayana.desc: Called the 'Great Vehicle', Mahāyāna is a branch of $buddhist$ that accepts not only the early $buddhist_ADJ$ text, but also those known as the Mahāyāna $sutra$. It emphasizes the figure of the $bodhisattva$, understanding the $bodhisattva$ path as available to all as a way to achieve Buddhahood. While originally developing in $india$, it saw much of its expansion through $china$ and the Silk Road, and the $chinese_group$ Canon forms now the basis of all $mahayana$.

shinto.name: Shintō
shinto.desc: The diverse set of beliefs and practices revolving around Kami worship that were present in $japan_region$ before the arrival of $buddhist$ got intrinsically tied to and blended with $buddhist_ADJ$ practices and concepts as $buddhist$ spread through $japan_region$. The Kami and $buddhist_ADJ$ deities were identified with one another, with both sets of beliefs becoming functionally inseparable. This gave rise to a particularly $japanese_group$ flavor of $buddhist$ blended with a $buddhist$-influenced Kami worship.

theravada.name: Theravāda
theravada.desc: Called 'School of the Elders', it adheres to the oldest traditions of $buddhist$. It rejects the Mahāyāna $sutra$ and thus the many $bodhisattva$ and the $bodhisattva$ path itself as being available to all. Instead, it focuses on the monastic community as the superior way of achieving enlightenment.

sammitiya.name: Saṃmitīya
sammitiya.desc: One of the many branches of early $buddhist$ in $india$, $sammitiya$ developed in $sindh_area$ becoming a great center of early $buddhist_ADJ$ schools even rivaling the Mahāyāna Nālandā. Being the biggest non-Mahāyāna $buddhist$ in $india$, it was removed from its place of prominence with the $muslim_ADJ$ invasions.

tibetan_buddhism.name: Tibetan Buddhism
tibetan_buddhism.desc: The form of $buddhist$ developed along and around the mountains of the Himalayas emerged from the Mahāyāna tradition, but incorporated many of the esoteric practices of Vajrayāna due to its close contact with India and the later stages of development of $buddhist$ there.

sanjiao.name: Sānjiào
sanjiao.desc: Called the 'Three Teachings', it is the combined blend and influences of $confucianism_policy$, $daoism_policy$, and $buddhist$. Being all three present in $china$ for centuries, and also influencing and being influenced by many other $chinese_group$ folk beliefs and deities, they have not always been in harmony among each other, but they have always been part of the $chinese_group$ way of life.

anglican.name: Anglicanism
anglican.desc: $anglican$ is a form of $christian$ in which the head of state is also the Supreme Governor of the Church. Theologically and institutionally, $anglican$ retains many elements of $catholic$ while also being influenced by Reformed Puritans and continental $lutheran_ADJ$ beliefs.

bogomilism.name: Bogomilism
bogomilism.desc: A neo-gnostic and dualist branch of $christian$, $bogomilism$ teaches that existence is divided between a spiritual realm and a material one. Its followers view their bodies as sacred temples and strive for closeness to God through purification rituals. These practices include fasting, dancing, and rejecting material excess to focus on spiritual growth.

bosnian_church.name: Krstjani
bosnian_church.desc: A breakaway sect of the $catholic_ADJ$ Church, the $bosnian_church$ developed its distinct theology due to prolonged isolation from mainstream Christianity. It focused heavily on apocalyptic themes, embraced mysticism, and retained many archaic practices of early $christian$. These traits led both $catholic_ADJ$ and $orthodox_ADJ$ authorities to denounce it as heretical.

calvinist.name: Calvinism
calvinist.desc: Named after John Calvin, $calvinist$ is a significant branch of Protestantism rooted in the principles of simplicity in worship and the supremacy of the Holy Bible. Its doctrine emphasizes predestination, asserting that God has preordained the destiny of all creation.

catharism.name: Catharism
catharism.desc: $catharism$ is a dualist movement that believes in the existence of two Gods: a benevolent God of Heaven and a malevolent counterpart. Its adherents follow an ascetic lifestyle, holding that souls are trapped in physical bodies as part of a cosmic struggle. Spiritual purification, achieved through strict discipline, is seen as the only path to salvation.

catholic.name: Catholicism
catholic.desc: Rooted in the Nicene Creed, $catholic$ is the largest denomination of $christian$ and is led by the Pope, who serves as the spiritual successor to Saint Peter. The Pope acts as both the head of the Church and a mediator in conflicts among $christian_ADJ$ rulers. Its doctrine and traditions have shaped much of the Western world's religious and cultural history.

hussite.name: Hussitism
hussite.desc: Founded by Jan Hus, the $hussite_ADJ$ Church emerged as a proto-Protestant movement in $BOH$, blending elements of the $BYZ_ADJ$ Rite with the teachings of John Wycliffe. It emphasized communion under both kinds and the importance of scripture over Church tradition.

lollardy.name: Lollardy
lollardy.desc: Led by John Wycliffe, $lollardy$ was a reformist movement advocating for universal priesthood and rejecting the necessity of sacraments like baptism and confession for salvation. Its teachings emphasized direct access to God through scripture, which was translated into vernacular languages. This made its theology accessible to the common people and fueled early calls for Church reform.

lutheran.name: Lutheranism
lutheran.desc: Based on Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses, $lutheran$ began as a call to reform the $catholic_ADJ$ Church but evolved into a distinct Protestant denomination. It teaches that the Old and New Testament scriptures are the sole infallible authority for $christian_ADJ$ doctrine.

miaphysite.name: Miaphysitism
miaphysite.desc: $miaphysite$ teaches that in the person of Christ, His divine and human natures are united into a single, indivisible nature. This doctrine, rooted in the Council of Ephesus, spread widely across regions like Armenia, Egypt, and Ethiopia. $miaphysite_ADJ$ communities have preserved their unique liturgies and traditions, emphasizing Christ's unity as both God and man.

nestorianism.name: Nestorianism
nestorianism.desc: $nestorianism$, named after Nestorius, teaches that Christ's divine and human natures are distinct and exist side by side. This doctrine was rejected by the Council of Ephesus but found a strong following in Persia and beyond. Nestorian Christians spread their faith across $asia$, becoming the largest $christian_ADJ$ religion in land area covered.

orthodox.name: Orthodoxy
orthodox.desc: The $orthodox_ADJ$ Church, rooted in the traditions of the early $christian_ADJ$ councils, emphasizes the continuity of apostolic teachings and sacred tradition. Centered on the $BYZ_ADJ$ Rite, it places great importance on liturgy, icons, and mysticism. The $orthodox_ADJ$ faith is led by patriarchs, with the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople holding a primacy of honor.

paulicianism.name: Paulicianism
paulicianism.desc: $paulicianism$ is a dualist $christian_ADJ$ sect that rejects the material world as the creation of an evil force. Its followers hold that only the spiritual realm is pure and base their beliefs on the New Testament, rejecting the Old Testament entirely. Persecuted by both $catholic_ADJ$ and $orthodox_ADJ$ authorities, the $paulicianism_ADJ$ movement resisted assimilation and inspired later reformist movements.

strigolniki.name: Strigolnichestvo
strigolniki.desc: Emerging in medieval $russian_region$, the $strigolniki$ is a reformist sect critical of the established $orthodox_ADJ$ Church. They condemn the corruption of priests, the selling of sacraments, and the accumulation of wealth by clergy. Favoring a simpler faith focused on personal piety, the $strigolniki_ADJ$ are a target by the $orthodox_ADJ$ Church and state authorities.

waldensian.name: Waldensian
waldensian.desc: Founded by Peter Waldo, the $waldensian$ is a reformist $christian_ADJ$ movement emphasizing simplicity, poverty, and the authority of scripture. They reject clerical wealth, the veneration of saints, and the necessity of sacraments for salvation. Persecuted as heretics, the $waldensian_ADJ$ movement have endured centuries of oppression while spreading their message across $europe$.

hindu.name: Hinduism
hindu.desc: A collection of different beliefs rather than a unified religion, $hindu$ is often considered the oldest religious tradition in the world. All its beliefs and practices understood as explanations of the $dharmic$, the cosmic order, it stems from the ancient Vedic literature. Being so varied, it also contains a multitude of gods, although not all of them are equally venerated or even recognized by all $hindu_ADJ$ practitioners, depending on their particular beliefs and orientations. The four main branches of $hindu$ are $vaishnavism$, $shaktism$, $shaivism$, and $smartism$.

jain.name: Jainism
jain.desc: One of the oldest religions, $jain$ is an Indian $dharmic_ADJ$ religion focusing on attempting self-realization and liberation from the cycle of death and rebirth. It centers in non-violence and asceticism through the teachings of the Tīrthaṅkara, the supreme preachers of the $dharma$, and it is divided in the Digambara and Śvetāmbara schools. Digambara, meaning 'sky-clad', is characterized by its rejection to attachment and possession of material goods, and thus its monks do not wear any clothes, and its iconography is more plain. Śvetāmbara, on the other hand, means 'white-clad' due to the white clothes of its monks, and has more equality between male and female monks, in opposition to the more male-oriented Digambara.

sikhism.name: Sikhism
sikhism.desc: A religion founded by the teachings of the $character_title_guru$, it originates from the varied $hindu_ADJ$ faiths of $india$, and incorporates many influences from $muslim$. It believes in one creator, $sikhism_god_name$, and to conduct oneself honestly and selflessly for the benefit of all. It encourages connection with the divine through the use of contemplation and meditation, as well as recitation and music as ways to be conscious of God's presence.

druzism.name: Druzism
druzism.desc: Although emerging from $ismaili_school$, $druzism_ADJ$ people do not consider themselves $muslim_ADJ$. Besides its obvious influence from $muslim$, it also gets influence from other Abrahamic and non-Abrahamic religions, giving rise to a distinct faith with emphasis on esotericism and the Cosmic Mind which all souls reunite to after many reincarnations.

shamanism.name: Shamanism
shamanism.desc: A shared set of practices and beliefs centering of the figure of the shaman, and individual capable of interacting with the spirit world and access the spirits or the spiritual energy to afect the physical world. Its specifics of spirits, gods, or rituals may vary, but the core concept of the spiritual world and its interactions with the material world remains in all $shamanism_ADJ$ practices.

tengri.name: Tengrism
tengri.desc: $tengri$ is a type of $shamanism_ADJ$ beliefs of the $turkic_group$ and $mongolian_group$ peoples, centered around the presence of the sky god $tengri_god_name$, who is worshiped as a personification of the universe. However, it also includes other deities, as it reveres nature and the deities that live in it, as well as the ancestors.

norse.name: Norse Paganism
norse.desc: The old religion of the $germanic_language_family$ of $scandinavian_region$, it includes a wide array of gods as the Æsir and Vanir, including the most famous Óðinn and Þórr. It considers the universe as nine different realms in the world tree Yggdrasill, of which Miðgarðr is the one in which humans live.

romuva.name: Romuva
romuva.desc: The traditional beliefs of the $lithuanian_group$ people, it contains a whole pantheon of gods, as well as reverence for nature and the ancestors. Its ceremonies are performed with fire altars, around which ritual hymns or dainos are sung.

sapmi_shamanism.name: Sámi Shamanism
sapmi_shamanism.desc: The traditional religions practices of the $sapmi$ people, it contains a multitude of natural and animal spirits, as well as veneration of the dead. Some of the animals are particularly revered, like reindeer and bears.

muinaisusko.name: Muinaisusko
muinaisusko.desc: The traditional beliefs of the $finnish_language$ peoples, it contains a multitude of deities, being the most prevalent one the sky and thunder god Ukko. It also contains veneration of the dead and shamanistic practices, while also sharing some features with other nearby religions.

inti.name: Inti
inti.desc: $inti_god$, together with $viracocha$, are the main gods that guide and protect the people of the $andes_region$

judaism.name: Judaism
judaism.desc: The original Abrahamic faith, $judaism$ adheres to the covenant made between God and Moses. The $judaism_ADJ$ Bible is the Tānāḵ, of which the first five books are known as the Tōrā, serving as the basis of all $judaism_ADJ$ faith and practice.

samaritanism.name: Samaritanism
samaritanism.desc: The traditional faith of the $samaritan_culture$, it emerged from $judaism$ after the fall of the Kingdom of Israel. $samaritanism$ considers itself to be the unchanged faith of the $israelite_group$ people from the times of Moses, in contrast to what they believe is a corruption of the scriptures by $judaism$.

mandeaism.name: Mandaeaism
mandeaism.desc: A gnostic religion considering John the Baptist to be the final prophet, $mandeaism$ also includes $greek_culture$ and $iranian_group$ influences. Although it considers as such some prophets of other Abrahamic religions, it does not consider Abraham, Moses, or Jesus to be $mandeaism_ADJ$ prophets. The God of $mandeaism$ is called $mandeaism_god_name$, meaning 'Great Life', and it represents the creative force of the universe.

manichaeism.name: Manichaeism
manichaeism.desc: $manichaeism$ is an $iranian_group$ religion founded by the prophet Mani in the Sasanian Empire. It has influences by many other religions, including Gnosticism, $zoroastrian$, $christian$, and $buddhist$ among others, but considers Mani to be the final prophet after Zoroaster, Buddha, and Jesus. Its theology is dualistic, describing the universe as a spiritual struggle between light and darkness.

shia.name: Shiism
shia.desc: The basis of the $shia_ADJ$ faith is that Muḥammad designated 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib as his successor as the spiritual and political leader of $muslim$. As such, the $imamate$ is to follow 'Alī's line rather than the one established by 'Abū Bakr when he was chosen as $rank_empire_muslim_ruler_male$ at the meeting of Saqīfah by the companions of Muḥammad.

sunni.name: Sunnism
sunni.desc: $sunni$ holds that the leadership of $muslim$ was passed to 'Abū Bakr when he was chosen as $rank_empire_muslim_ruler_male$ at the meeting of Saqīfah by the companions of Muḥammad, as the Prophet himself did not appoint any successor. It thus reveres the al-Rāshidūn, the first four $rank_empire_muslim_ruler_male$ after Muḥammad, as a model of governance.

nahuatl.name: Nahua
nahuatl.desc: The religion of the $nahua_group$, in which the many $nahuatl_god_name$ or gods are organized under the supreme god Ōmeteōtl. Many other gods, like $huitzilopochtli_god$, $tlaloc_god$, or $quetzalcoatl_god$ are commonly adopted as patron of estates or peoples. One of its key practices is that of human sacrifice, performed in honor of the gods and a necessity to keep their favor.

yazidism.name: Yazidism
yazidism.desc: Emerging from an $iranian_group$ tradition, it also contains elements from $judaism$, $christian$, and $muslim$. It beliefs that the universe was created by God but that he appointed the 'Peacock Angel' Tawûsî Melek to rule over it. Although it contains many influences by other religions, especially in its esoteric practices, its core is rooted in the ancient $iranian_group$ religions.

zoroastrian.name: Zoroastrianism
zoroastrian.desc: An ancient $iranian_group$ religion following the teachings of Zoroaster, also called Zarathustra, and the texts of the Avesta. It is based on a dualistic cosmology of good and evil, with the eternal conflict of the deity Ahura Mazdā and the destructive spirit Angra Mainyu, with a predicted ultimate triumph of good over evil.

common_folk_religion_desc.name: religion refers to the indigenous beliefs, mythology, traditions, and practices maintained and transmitted by its followers since the beginning of time.

ibadi_school_desc.name: Believed to be a descendant of the Al-Khawārij, who first were supporters of 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib but later rejected his arbitration. The school distanced itself from the Al-Khawārij following 'Abd Allāh ibn Ibāḍ, taking a more moderate approach and a more positive view towards different branches, having similarities with many of the other schools.

_mechanic_descs.has_karma: Karma is measured on a scale from -100 to +100, and reflects the past deeds of a Country. A Country will benefit the most when its Karma is in Balance, between -33 and +33.
_mechanic_descs.has_purity: It is the indication of how pure our Country is according to Shintō. Purity is lost by contact with anything impure, such as killing and losing People in Battles, or epidemics, as death and blood are impure. It is gained through performing religious acts, such as pilgrimages to Holy Sites or ritual suicide.
_mechanic_descs.has_honor: How honorable our Country is in the eyes of our People. Maintaining the Purity of our Country above 75 will increase our Honor while having low Purity will decrease it. Other religious and Diplomatic Actions may also affect it.
_mechanic_descs.has_yanantin: Yanantin represents the Balance between two complementary but opposing entities. Following the mindset of the andean group Cultures, Harmony can only be achieved when a being, a man, darkness, the Sun, finds its complement and joins it, a woman, light, the Moon.
_mechanic_descs.has_religious_influence: It is a value of the Ability that a Country has to interact with and influence matters of its Primary Religion. Depending on the Religion, the uses it will have will be different, as well as the ways for a Country to acquire it.
_mechanic_descs.has_canonization: A former Ruler of a Country can be Canonized, that is, made into a Saint. This will confer upon the Country extra benefits, scaled according to how able the Character was when they were alive.
_mechanic_descs.has_religious_head: It is the Character considered to be in charge, and representative of, a whole Religion denomination.
_mechanic_descs.has_rite_power: This is a value of the Ability that a Country that is the Leader of its Autocephalous Patriarchate has to modify its Religion through the selection of various of its Laws.
_mechanic_descs.needs_reform: Catholicism Religion has internal conflicts between what is the correct doctrine or not, and about what is part of the Faith or not. As time goes by, the desire to Reform becomes bigger, and will impact any future discussion about the doctrine of Catholicism.
